name: Mustard Green
lede: Mustard Green is a sharp, acid yellow-green named for the condiment, almost identical on screen to Acid Green and rare in our painting archive.

sections.title: A condiment word
sections.body:
The library records Mustard Green only from the xkcd 2010 crowd survey, so an earlier coining of this exact compound is undocumented, though *mustard* itself is a much older color word built on the plant and condiment [1]. At hex #A8B504 it measures lightness 70 and chroma 75 in LCH, a bright, acid green-yellow [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[acid-green|Acid Green]], only 2.7 CIEDE2000 units away and read as almost the same color, followed closely by [[acid-green|Bright Olive]] at 3.8 [2]. The library separately logs Bile and Acid Green as near-duplicate crowd names [1]. Werner's 1821 nomenclature lists a snapdragon variety used for Sulphur Yellow, 8.2 units off, and the nearest gem comparison is common [[gem:peridot|peridot]], 9.0 units away [2][3]. It reads as a much sharper, more acid color than plain [[olive|Olive]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color is one of the rarest in our archive, matching only 3 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.01%, as photographed, rarer than 77% of the named colors here [4]. The earliest is a 1888 painting by Paul Sérusier, and the other two date from around 1900, so every match here comes from the same narrow window [4]. That is too thin a sample for a reliable painter or country reading, and these are photographs of aged, varnished canvases, so a match is not a pigment test [4].
